allies.rationale_text: Cognitive-load-theory supports schema-acquisition by reducing working-memory strain so chunking and scaffolding can build stable mental structure.
allies.source_quote: CLT emphasizes optimizing the learning environment to reduce strain on working memory, which frees up capacity for the encoding process necessary for schema formation.
allies.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'CLT emphasizes optimizing the learning environment to reduce strain on working memory, which frees up capacity for the encoding process necessary for schema formation.'
allies.activation_condition: When reducing cognitive load is needed to free working memory capacity for the encoding process that builds durable schemas.

allies.rationale_text: Abstraction helps schema-acquisition compress detail into a usable map without losing the underlying structure people need to retrieve later.
allies.source_quote: Schemas are conceptual maps-deliberately organized, abstracted, and simplified visions of a complex intellectual landscape.
allies.affinity_rationale: Moderate: schemas ARE abstractions — 'deliberately organized, abstracted, and simplified visions of a complex intellectual landscape.' Schema acquisition is the process of building useful abstractions.
allies.activation_condition: When building mental models requires abstracting complex reality into simplified, organized representations that enable pattern recognition.

antagonists.rationale_text: Einstellung-effect undermines schema-acquisition by causing the learner to persist with the first recognized pattern instead of encoding a better-fitting schema for the novel situation.
antagonists.source_quote: Cognitive Entrenchment (The 'Seen This Before' Error): Assuming that a genuinely novel problem is merely a variation of a problem solved previously, causing problem solvers to incorrectly persist in using unhelpful or misleading schemas.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Canonical (as Availability Heuristic): 'prevents deliberate schema acquisition by substituting a simpler, known model for the complex actual model needed.'
antagonists.activation_condition: When familiar schemas are applied reflexively to novel problems, preventing acquisition of more appropriate new schemas.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Schema-acquisition conflicts with representativeness-heuristic when familiar pattern labels replace context-specific diagnosis.
structured_tensions.source_quote: schema-acquisition vs representativeness-heuristic: schema-acquisition conflicts with representativeness-heuristic (representativeness bias) when familiar pattern labels replace context-specific diagnosis.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Schema-acquisition conflicts with first-principles-thinking when overlearned templates block reconstruction from base facts.
structured_tensions.source_quote: schema-acquisition vs first-principles-thinking: schema-acquisition conflicts with first-principles-thinking (first principles thinking) when overlearned templates block reconstruction from base facts.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Schema-acquisition conflicts with anchoring when the first schema encountered creates a reference point that distorts evaluation of a better-fitting schema.
structured_tensions.source_quote: schema-acquisition vs anchoring: schema-acquisition conflicts with anchoring (anchoring) when the first schema encountered creates a reference point that distorts the evaluation of subsequent, potentially better-fitting schemas.
